Name: Shannon Tuley
Badge: Teacher as Researcher: Cultivating Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

I learned that I can and am good at adapting lessons to fit the needs of my classroom. I started Say Mean Matter as a bell ringer. Some of my higher functioning kids were able to write what the quote said, translate the meaning in their own words, and explain why it matters with ease, and didn't have any questions. Others looked at the board with confusion. Once I explained it, they were fine, and the quote/activity opened up a very meaningful discussion along with real world connections. I administered this activity in a more formal way with the worksheet provided in the modules and it worked out much better. The students' writings were much more organized this way. I also turned this into an activity to explore themes in the novel we were reading, which is different that how I usually teach them, but I like how it worked out! The connections my students made were fantastic!

Share one artifact or anecdote from trying out your chosen strategy (e.g., a piece of student work, notes from your Writer’s Notebook, a classroom snapshot, or a brief story from the experience).:
What new questions or next steps are you leaving this module with? How might you continue to explore or build on this inquiry in your future teaching?:

My next steps are to fit this activity in more often. I like that I can adapt it to a variety of texts, and I really loved using it to teach theme.
